record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal evaluations for released models after abliteration, bearing on practical refusal removal (V2). Heretic uses a parameterized weight-edit approach rather than the original activation ablation recipe.
record.gate_note: The README's residual-geometry table is presented as an example output for gemma-3-270m-it, not as a test of whether the direction causally mediates refusal. The README also describes parameter choices and features without reporting their separate effects; these are not rows.
record.test_reason: The README reports refusal counts for released weight-edited (abliterated) Gemma-3-12b-it models against the original. That bears on V2, practical removal of refusal by a weight edit. Heretic uses a parameterized, optimizer-tuned variant of directional weight orthogonalization rather than the original recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README says Heretic, run automatically with defaults, matches expert manual abliterations in refusal suppression (3/100) at much lower KL divergence (0.16), which it reads as less capability damage. It also concedes that metrics are no substitute for human evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo. Heretic orthogonalizes selected attention output-projection and MLP down-projection matrices against layer-associated refusal directions, with separately optimized ablation parameters and a flexible layer-weight kernel. The README describes this as a parameterized variant of directional ablation, not a reproduction of the original activation-projection method.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says ablation parameters are optimized separately for components, allows per-layer or interpolated direction indices, and says MLP interventions tend to be more damaging than attention interventions; it reports no separate evaluation results for these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On harmless prompts, the Heretic model's KL divergence from the original is 0.16, versus 1.04 and 0.45 for the other abliterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimized weight-kernel abliteration reaches the same refusal suppression with lower output-distribution divergence than manual abliterations.

record.problems: Evidence is README-reported and the code was not read or run. The README notes values may vary by platform and hardware. It does not specify the harmful or harmless prompt sets beyond the harmful sample count, refusal criteria, or uncertainty estimates. KL divergence is not a direct general-capability benchmark.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported results were omitted. User testimonials were not counted as study results. The example residual-geometry table and descriptions of parameter choices were not treated as intervention outcomes.

untested.parts: Capability retention under the edit (KL divergence only, no benchmarks); models beyond Gemma-3-12b-it (others are named only through user testimonials); the refusal-judging criterion.
No causal ablation or addition test reported; the residual-geometry table is an example output only.
Interpolated direction indices are described, but no result compares single versus multiple directions.

record.verdict_notes: This repo is a non-star copy of p-e-w/heretic, and its README table is the upstream author's result, so it is not independent evidence. Do not count it separately from p-e-w/heretic. Evidence is a single README table with no uncertainty, refusal criterion or prompt-set description, and values are said to be hardware-dependent. KL divergence is not a capability benchmark. User testimonials (GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen3-4B) are not results.

versions.untested_parts: No causal test of removing or adding the direction, and no general-capability evaluation.
The README reports refusal counts for released abliterated models, but does not state the exact weight-edit settings or evaluate general capabilities directly.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
The README describes interpolating directions but reports no result testing whether refusal requires multiple directions.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from refusal.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No test of how or when refusal training affects the direction.

statements.correction: Heretic README table on Gemma-3-12b-it: original 97/100 refusals; mlabonne-v2 3/100 (KL 1.04); huihui-ai 3/100 (KL 0.45); p-e-w heretic 3/100 (KL 0.16). Optimizer: TPE (Optuna), co-minimizing refusals and KL. Held-out status of the prompts is not stated.
statements.problem: Small nuance only. Heretic's objective co-minimizes refusals and KL divergence, not refusals alone. The held-out caveat applies only to the Heretic checkpoint (r4). The other two checkpoints are third-party manual abliterations, and the README does not give their recipes.
